terrain.label: Terrain
terrain.detail: Adaptive hypsometric tint. Deep-sea blue → shallow cyan → lowland green → highland brown → snow white. Mutually exclusive with other thematic layers. On by default.

landsea.label: Land/Sea
landsea.detail: Binary blue/green shading to quickly distinguish ocean from land. Mutually exclusive with other thematic layers.

plates.label: Plates
plates.detail: Each tectonic plate is colored distinctly. Plates are generated by the Cortial (2019) spherical Voronoi partition — Poisson-disc seeds + synchronized BFS. Colors cycle from a 15-color palette. Can stack over any base/thematic layer.

boundaries.label: Crust & Boundaries
boundaries.detail: Plate interiors colored by crust type: continental = warm brown, oceanic = grey-blue, transitional = olive. Hotspot chains = magenta. Ancient orogenies = dark gold. Rifts = cyan. Boundaries by type: convergent = red (subduction/collision), divergent = green (ridges/rifts), transform = yellow (strike-slip). Feature lines always on top.

koppen.label: Köppen Climate
koppen.detail: Colored by Köppen-Geiger climate class. A=tropical(blue)·B=arid(red/orange)·C=temperate(green/yellow)·D=continental(purple/cyan)·E=polar(grey)·Ocean=deep blue. Mutually exclusive with other thematic layers (single thematic slot, radio).

temperature.label: Temperature
temperature.detail: Annual mean temperature (°C) diverging scale. Fixed physical range −40…+40°C, with 0°C (freezing) at the midpoint — cold deep blue, 0°C white, hot deep red. Comparable across worlds; ocean transparent. Mutually exclusive with other thematic layers (radio).

precipitation.label: Precipitation
precipitation.detail: Annual precipitation (mm/yr) sequential scale, log-normalized (0…30000mm) because precipitation spans five orders of magnitude. Pale yellow=dry(0mm)→yellow-green=~100mm→blue-green=~1000mm→deep blue=wet(>10000mm). Ocean transparent. Mutually exclusive (radio).

biomes.label: Whittaker Biomes
biomes.detail: Whittaker (1975) temperature-precipitation two-axis classification. Tropical rainforest=deep green·savanna=pale yellow-green·desert=beige·temperate forest=mid green·grassland=gold·boreal=blue-grey·tundra=grey-brown·ice=white·ocean=deep blue. Mutually exclusive with Köppen (one of four).

npp.label: Net Primary Productivity
npp.desc: NPP heatmap (Miami model, warm beige→deep green)
npp.detail: Net primary productivity from the Miami model (Lieth 1975). Warm beige=low (desert <200) → deep green=high (rainforest >2000). Normalized to 0–3000 gC/m²/yr.

domesticable.label: Domestication Potential
domesticable.detail: Domestication potential via Whittaker biome lookup (Diamond 1997 framework). Gold=high herbivores+high crops·orange=high herbivores only·light green=high crops only·transparent=low. Temperate grassland is all-high.

soil.label: Soil Type
soil.detail: USDA soil orders derived from parent rock + climate (temperature/precipitation). Mollisol=deep green (temperate grassland, fertile)·Alfisol=olive·Oxisol/Ultisol=red (tropical/subtropical weathering, poor)·Aridisol=yellow·Spodosol/Gelisol=grey·Inceptisol/Entisol=light grey (young soils). Fertility feeds agricultural potential.

provinces.label: Biogeographic Provinces
provinces.detail: Two-level division by continental connectivity (realm) + contiguous biome (province). Colors cycle from the plate palette; same color = same province. References Wallace/Udvardy regionalization.

habitable.label: Habitability Grade
habitable.detail: Habitability grade = a 0–100 product of an asymmetric human-climate-niche band (peak 13 °C, Xu 2020) and an aridity ramp. Coastal access is an orthogonal dimension (distance_to_coast_km), not part of the score. Dark = polar/arid · brown = marginal · amber = moderate · green = good · teal = excellent temperate-humid. No hard zero — cool-wet oceanic ET (Faroese-type) sits mid-range: liveable but not farmable. Mutually exclusive (radio).

agriculture.label: Agriculture Grade
agriculture.detail: Agriculture grade = a hard zero below the Köppen C/D tree-line (warmest month >10°C), then a product of growing-degree-day (base 10°C, McMaster 1997), water, and soil-fertility factors. Grey = no crops · beige = marginal · yellow = moderate · gold = excellent farmland. Independent of habitability. Mutually exclusive (radio).

flow.label: Drainage
flow.detail: Upstream catchment area (km²) sequential scale, log-normalised (dynamic max). Navy=headwaters/small basins → blue → light blue → white=continental trunk. Shows where surface water concentrates and basin structure. Closed inland lakes are shown in light cyan; ocean transparent. Freely stackable over any layer.

currents.label: Ocean Currents
currents.detail: Surface flow field from the Stommel wind-driven circulation model. Direction=flow, length∝speed, magenta=warm·cyan=cold. Sampled on a ~8° grid, crisp at any zoom. Freely stackable.

winds.label: Winds
winds.detail: Near-surface wind field from three-cell circulation + geostrophic wind. Direction=wind, length∝speed, color=temperature (blue=−20°C→green=0°C→red=+35°C). Shows heat transport / cold-air paths. Sampled on a ~8° grid.

coastlines.label: Coastlines
coastlines.detail: Cells within ±200m of sea level rendered as a light grey-blue outline, stacked above all thematic layers to help locate land/sea boundaries in layers lacking terrain reference (NPP, domestication). On by default.

rivers.label: Rivers
rivers.detail: Vector polylines of the hydrology river network (backend features layer): only channels above the resolution-independent catchment threshold are drawn, with stroke width increasing by stream order. Cartographic approach — visible rivers at 51 km cells come from vector lines, not DEM incision. On by default.

drag.description: Pan the map (2D) / rotate the globe (3D)

nKey.description: 3D globe view: reset to default camera (north pole up, equator facing you).

sunTime.description: Adjust subsolar longitude (diurnal, 0° = noon on the prime meridian), i.e. the day/night terminator position. Requires the lighting toggle on (off by default).

sunSeason.description: Adjust orbital position (annual, 0° = vernal equinox, 90° = N. summer solstice). Combined with axial tilt it moves the subsolar latitude, tilting the terminator seasonally (midnight sun / polar night). Planets without tilt have no seasons. Supported on all 2D projections and the 3D globe.

sunToggle.description: 2D/3D left panel: turn day/night lighting on/off (off by default). GPU-driven on both 2D and 3D. Settings synced via URL (?sun=&season=&night=) and shareable across 2D↔3D.

debugReproject.description: Append ?reproject=cpu to force the legacy CPU reprojection for Mollweide/Robinson, to compare against the GPU result. Debug only — the main map always requires WebGL; this is not a no-GPU fallback.

hoverCell.description: The right panel shows cell properties; selected cells take priority if any.

hoverLeave.description: Restores the planet summary when no cell is selected; the panel locks (no jump back) when a cell is selected.

ctrlClick.description: Append/remove from the selection (keeps existing). Standard desktop-app style.

dblClick.description: Select that cell (clearing others); deselect if it is already the only selection.

clickPlanet.description: In the 3D stellar view, opens the info panel. Expand "🌍 Terrain data" for a summary if available.

dblClickPlanet.description: In the 3D stellar view, flies the camera to that planet.

equirectangular.label: Equirectangular
equirectangular.description: Orthogonal graticule, polar stretching. The simplest projection, good for data processing.

mollweide.label: Mollweide
mollweide.description: Equal-area pseudo-cylindrical, elliptical outline. Good for area comparison.

robinson.label: Robinson
robinson.description: Compromise projection, visually comfortable. Common in National Geographic-style publications.

dag.title: DAG Layer Architecture
dag.summary: World data is organized by discipline: physics → chemistry → astronomy → geological → climate → ecology → civilization. Upstream layer inputs drive downstream layer outputs, forming a directed acyclic graph (DAG) simulation pipeline.

branch.title: Branch System
branch.summary: Like a Git branch. Forks at a DAG layer, sharing all data above it and storing only the fork layer and below. Different branches of the same planet can have different land/sea distributions, climates, or civilizations.

cvt.title: CVT Spherical Mesh
cvt.summary: Centroidal Voronoi Tessellation — a uniform spherical mesh via Fibonacci spiral + Lloyd relaxation. All simulation (tectonics, climate, hydrology) runs directly on the spherical mesh, projected to a 2D raster only at final visualization.

cortial.title: Cortial 2019 Plate Tectonics
cortial.summary: Plate partition and evolution follow Cortial et al. (2019) Procedural Tectonic Planets: Poisson-disc seeds → spherical Voronoi partition → Euler-pole rotation → boundary re-detection → subduction/collision/erosion. See terrain-pipeline.md.

entries.title: Create a world
entries.content:
`dreamulator init <name> --template earthlike`

Create a new world from a template. Available templates: `minimal` (minimal config), `earthlike` (Earth-like planet).

entries.title: Run the simulation
entries.content:
`dreamulator build <world>`

Run all engines in DAG order: astronomy → geology (terrain+plates) → climate → ecology.

`dreamulator build <world> --only climate`

Run only the specified layer and any not-yet-run predecessors.

`dreamulator build <world> --force`

Force re-run all engines even if outputs already exist.

entries.title: Terrain generation
entries.content:
`dreamulator terrain generate <world> -p <planet> -n 100000 --seed 42`

Generate CVT mesh + plate partition + tectonic evolution + terrain synthesis + raster export.

`dreamulator terrain generate <world> -p <planet> -n 4096`

Low resolution for fast iteration (~30 s vs ~100 s at 100k).

`dreamulator terrain generate <world> -p <planet> --tectonic-steps 125`

Time-evolution steps (2 My each; default 50 = 100 My).

`dreamulator terrain info <world> -p <planet>`

View the terrain summary (land/sea ratio, elevation stats).

entries.title: Start the server
entries.content:
`dreamulator serve --open`

Start the FastAPI server and open the browser. See README for Vite HMR dev mode.

`dreamulator serve --data-dir <path>`

Use a custom data directory.

entries.title: Branch management
entries.content:
`dreamulator branch create <world> <name> --at <layer>`

Fork a branch at a layer. E.g. `--at geological` → different land/sea under the same astronomy.

`dreamulator branch list <world>`

List all branches.

`dreamulator build <world> --branch <name>`

Run on a branch.

`dreamulator branch promote <world> <name> --as <new-world>`

Promote a branch to an independent world.

entries.title: Climate validation
entries.content:
`dreamulator climate validate <world>`

Validate climate accuracy against real Earth observations (Köppen group accuracy, precipitation RMSE, Cohen's Kappa). Requires ETOPO1 elevation data.

entries.title: AI narration
entries.content:
`dreamulator narrate <world>`

Generate a colloquial world description via the Claude API.

`dreamulator narrate <world> --branch <name>`

Narrate a specific branch.

`dreamulator narrate <world> -m <model>`

Specify an Anthropic model.

entries.title: Create a world
entries.content: Click "New World" on the "Worlds" page. Pick a template (`minimal` or `earthlike`), set a name and a random seed. The seed determines every procedural result — same seed + same input = an identical world.

entries.title: World structure
entries.content:
Each world organizes data by discipline:

```
physics → chemistry → astronomy → geological → climate → ecology → civilization
```

Each layer has `input/` (YAML, human-authored) and `derived/` (JSON, engine-computed). Engines read only from input and write only to derived — the LLM cannot "hallucinate" physics.

entries.title: Branch system
entries.content:
Branches are like Git branches. After forking at a DAG layer, they share all data above and store only the fork layer and below.

- Fork at `astronomy` → different star systems under the same physics
- Fork at `geological` → different land/sea under the same star system
- Fork at `climate` → different climate under the same geology

Branches switch via URL `?branch=<name>`, affecting all API queries and rendering.

entries.title: Build & validate
entries.content:
Click "Build" on the world detail page to run the pipeline. Build outputs include:

- `maps/<planet>/` — elevation, CVT mesh, plates, climate rasters
- `layers/<layer>/derived/` — engine results (JSON/YAML)
- `build_profile.json` — per-engine/per-stage timings

"Validate" checks world file integrity (schema, required fields).

entries.title: Basics
entries.content:
**Drag** — rotate
**Scroll** — zoom
**Right-drag** — pan

Click a planet to open the info panel (with terrain summary). Double-click a planet → fly the camera to it.

entries.title: Planet textures
entries.content: Planets with map data auto-load terrain textures, showing real land/sea colors (not solid spheres). Textures are decoded from elevation PNGs into low-res equirectangular maps.

entries.title: Habitable zone
entries.content: A green translucent ring marks the habitable zone (liquid water can exist on the surface). Inner/outer edges are computed from stellar luminosity + planetary albedo + greenhouse parameters.

entries.title: Planet info panel
entries.content:
Clicking a planet opens the InfoPanel:

- Orbital parameters (semi-major axis, eccentricity, period)
- Physical parameters (mass, radius, density)
- If map data exists: elevation range, sea level, cell count

entries.title: Basics
entries.content:
**Drag** — rotate
**Scroll** — zoom
**Right-drag / Ctrl+drag** — pan
**N key** — reset to default camera (north up, equator facing you)

**Ctrl+click** → append/remove a cell from the selection
**Double-click** → select a cell (clearing others); deselect if already the only one
**Esc** → clear all selections.

entries.title: Layer system
entries.content:
The left panel controls layer display, a four-slot compositing model:

1. **Base** — terrain shading (fixed)
2. **Thematic** — Köppen / Whittaker biomes / NPP / domestication (pick one)
3. **Fill** — plate shading (stacks over thematic)
4. **Feature** — boundaries, coastlines, current arrows (always on top)

Each layer has independent opacity. With no overlays the base is sampled directly at zero extra cost.

entries.title: Day/night lighting
entries.content:
Left-panel SunControl:

- **Lighting toggle** (off by default) — enables GPU day/night shading
- **Time slider** — subsolar longitude (diurnal)
- **Season slider** — orbital position (annual, needs axial tilt > 0)

Settings sync via URL (`?sun=&season=&night=`) across 2D↔3D.

entries.title: Cell inspector
entries.content:
The right panel switches by selection:

**0 selected** — shows the hovered cell (coords, elevation, crust, plate, climate); leaving → planet summary
**1 selected** — locks that cell (no jump back on mouse leave)
**>1 selected** — multi-select stats (count, area, elevation range/mean, mean temp/precip, dominant Köppen)

Selected cells highlight yellow; hovered cells highlight blue.

entries.title: Overview
entries.content: CivMap overlays fictional territorial coloring on a real Earth administrative base map. Leaflet renders GeoJSON boundaries with ADM0 (country) / ADM1 (province) levels.

entries.title: Basics
entries.content:
**Click a country** — select and highlight its borders
**Paint mode** — pick a color and click a country to paint (simulate territorial division)
**Snapshots** — create/switch time snapshots, each saving the territorial assignments at that time

Data lives in GeoJSON + LFS, with branch inheritance.
